newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peronists choose governor's wife for key election.
newsitem.headline: Peronists choose governor's wife for key election.

text.p: Argentina's Peronists have chosen a governor's wife who runs an army of women that feeds thousands of poor people to fight Congressional elections in October -- the first battle for the presidency in 1999.

The opposition reacted with dismay and mockery on Tuesday to news that Gov. Eduardo Duhalde of Buenos Aires Province, by far Argentina's biggest constituency with 8 million voters, had persuaded his wife, Hilda, to run for Congress and head Peronist candidates for deputy of the province.

Known as Chiche or simply "La senora," she has a huge following in the traditionally Peronist province, where her 17,000 women volunteers dish out milk and food to 600,000 people a day, mostly pregnant women and children.

Her actions among the poor, helped by a huge budget from the province of $280 million a year, have earned inevitable comparisons with Eva Peron. However, she has displayed none of the glamour and charisma that earned Evita mythical status.
"I have never been a housewife but neither am I an intellectual. I am a Peronist by sentiment and conviction," said the former schoolteacher in one recent interview.
The charity is matched by an iron will that does not shy from criticising even President Carlos Menem: "If I had to make one criticism, I'd tell him to strengthen the network of social protection."
With unemployment over 17 percent, this makes her a formidable opponent in October's elections. Menem, realising that, has pushed Duhalde to persuade her to run for months.
For Duhalde himself, a victory for his wife would boost his chances of succeeding Menem as president in 1999.
"It was what I expected," was Menem's comment on Tuesday on her candidacy, which makes history by turning the polling in the province into a contest between two women.
Her main rival is 66-year-old centre-left Sen. Graciela Fernandez Meijide, who lost a son to the death squads in the 1970s and is winning hearts with her straight-talking style.
Her first shot was to demand that her 50-year-old rival resign from the province's Social Action Secretariat, with its huge budget, as a "matter of minimum ethics."

The latest opinion polls, compiled before Hilda Duhalde decided to run, give Fernandez Meijide a wide lead. But the fight could be a close one because of the Peronists' unrivaled grass roots organisation in the province.
"It's going to be tough fighting both of them," said Radical Party candidate and former President Raul Alfonsin.

Other opponents said the Peronists chose Duhalde because it had no other strong runners. "It is a sign of weakness, not strength," said Radical deputy Federico Storani. "It's clear that the other candidates were a risk for the Peronists."
